content.text: A single five-second real-time live-action insert, matching this exact ground-level composition. Locked camera; charcoal and timber never move. Heavy raindrops fall visibly DOWNWARD throughout, strike the charcoal, and splash naturally. The small muddy rivulet at left steadily spreads a shallow finger of runoff RIGHTWARD into the charcoal depression. In the first two seconds, this thin water visibly touches and wets the FRONT small glowing charcoal first. The front ember crack becomes dark ONLY where water touches it. In seconds two to four, rain and runoff wet the REAR charcoal crack; its remaining dull orange glow shrinks gradually from bottom to top as the water contacts it. Tiny transparent local wisps at contact, no smoke cloud. Final second: both cracks fully dark, wet black charcoal remains sharply readable while rain and shallow runoff continue. Photographed physical water touching hot carbon, practical natural effects. There are NO open flames at any time, nothing is blown out, no gust of wind, no sudden global brightness change, no animation of the wood, no levitation, no burst, no sudden flood or large wave. No cut, no zoom, no slow motion. Muted natural neutral daylight, same exposure from beginning to end. Only real rain patter, shallow trickling water and a restrained short wet hiss at each contact. No voice, no speech, NO music.16:9.
